title: Field sell flow + USP snippets for inference (WIP)
content:
Slide 1 — one-line opener: Why inference decisions matter for product teams (30s)
- Speaker note: quick hook about how small infra choices change unit economics and UX. Use a customer quote if you have it.

Slide 2 — core value props (30s each)
- Predictable performance across hosted / dedicated / private
- Transparent cost controls (batching, quantization, routing)
- Observable rollouts and safe fallbacks (canary -> auto-fallback)
- Speaker note: say this as a checklist: speed, cost, reliability, compliance.

Slide 3 — The Serve Economics Ladder (new framing)
- Level 1: Prototype (low traffic) — use hosted API for speed to market
- Level 2: Scale with predictability — move to Dedicated/reserved pools
- Level 3: Regulated / data-sensitive — Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Quick seller lines: "We help you pick the ladder rung that reduces surprises and frees your engineers."

Slide 4 — Quick decision tree (use in discovery)
- Q1: Is data regulated or sensitive? -> Yes = Private, No -> Q2
- Q2: Do you need 99ms p50 or sub-500ms p95? -> Yes = Dedicated w/ latency SLO, No -> Hosted
- Q3: Is predictable monthly spend required? -> Yes = Reserved capacity
- Speaker note: read the tree aloud. Give a recommendation in <60s.

Slide 5 — ROI quick math (demo script)
- Inputs to ask for: expected tokens/day, peak qps, acceptable tail latency, security constraints
- Back-of-envelope: cost_per_month = tokens_per_day * 30 * (hosted_rate or reserved_unit_rate) + infra_premium_for_latency
- Seller tip: use conservative numbers to avoid oversell; offer to run a quick sizing exercise post-call.

Slide 6 — Objection handling (battlecard style)
- Objection: "We can just host our own models on cloud VMs."
  - Reply: "You can, but you take on kernel selection, batching, caching, and tail-smoothing. We bring proven runtime optimizations + routing and SLA."
- Objection: "Your hosted costs look high compared to raw GPUs."
  - Reply: "Compare total cost of ownership: model ops time, debuggering, perf regressions, and engineering hours. We optimize tokens and latency at the platform level."
- Objection: "We need air-gapped on-prem."
  - Reply: "We have a private package that integrates with customer KMS/HSM and audit logs; we can scope a POC."

Slide 7 — Metrics to cite (quick bullets sales can memorize)
- Typical hosted p50 latency: 60–120ms (varies by model and prompt length)
- Tail smoothing benefit: up to 40% reduction in p95 with smart batching + routing
- Cost delta: quantization + batching -> 20–60% unit cost reduction in many NLP workloads
- Note: customize with our model catalog numbers during prep.

Slide 8 — Live demo script (2-3 minute podium)
- 0:00–0:20 — quick product intro and value prop
- 0:20–0:90 — run a short streaming generation with tool calls and show latency/trace in console
- 1:30–2:00 — show routing config (hosted -> dedicated fallback) + rollout panel
- Seller tip: keep the demo resilient: pre-warm KV cache and use a short prompt to avoid cold-start confusion.

Slide 9 — Battlecard snippet: "Unit economics swap" technique
- Use when buyer fixesate on raw token price.
- Ask: "What's your current engineering spend per week for tuning/ops?"
- Show a 3-line comparison: (a) raw-cloud + ops hours vs (b) Redwood with reserved capacity + SLOs + support.
- Callout: emphasize time-to-repair and quality regressions avoided.

Slide 10 — Competitive talking points (concise)
- Against managed endpoints: we provide deeper runtime optimizations + predictable rollouts
- Against open-source self-host: we reduce engineering lift and ops headaches, and provide enterprise controls faster
- Against major cloud model APIs: focus on consistent SLA + cheaper reserved throughput at scale
- TODO: add competitor-specific data points (from ops/marketing)

Slide 11 — Suggested discovery questions (use in first 10 min)
- "What's your current inference architecture and pain points?"
- "How many inference requests/day and what does your peak look like?"
- "What latency numbers matter to your end user?"
- "Are there compliance or data residency needs?"

Slide 12 — Call / next steps templates (two options)
- Fast path: "We’ll run a sizing + 2-week trial on hosted and show expected cost/latency improvements."
- Enterprise path: "We’ll scope a Dedicated POC and design an SLA + onboarding plan; security team intro included."

Slide 13 — Appendix: quick checklist for solution engineers
- Get sample prompts and distribution of sequence lengths
- Ask for traffic patterns (diurnal, bursty) and tolerance for 95th pct latency
- Collect compliance constraints and key rotation policies
- Confirm acceptance criteria for POC (latency target, cost target, uptime)

Slide 14 — Open items / WIP (for this draft)
- Add actual model-level baseline numbers from bench team (action: Diego)
- Build a 90s demo script that never shows raw infra (action: Hannah)
- Create one-pager ROI worksheet for AE to email post-call (action: Samir)

Slide 15 — Speaker closing lines and one-liners to memorize
- "We make inference predictable so your product can be reliable."
- "You don’t buy GPUs; you buy predictable UX for your end users."
- Quick ask: "Can we run a two-week sizing to show you the numbers?"

Notes: rough, intentionally terse — this is a field-friendly slide set to be trimmed to 6–8 slides for customer meetings. Use this to draft a shorter deck for outbound cadences.

Questions / feedback welcome — especially missing competitor calls and real benchmark numbers that sales wants on hand.
